newsitem.title: UK: UK's Bodycote to buy Swedish Brukens.
newsitem.headline: UK's Bodycote to buy Swedish Brukens.

text.p: Britain's Bodycote International Plc said on Thursday it was to buy Swedish heat treatment group Brukens Thermotreat AB for 625 million Swedish crowns (57.5 million pounds, or $94.33 million) in cash.

Bodycote said it would finance the deal with a one-for-three rights issue of new shares at 600 pence per share. The share issue will raise 115.5 million pounds, with the extra funds for further small acquisitions and to refinance acquisitions already announced, Bodycote said in a statement.
Brukens is one of the largest heat treatment groups in Europe, with 27 plants, 10 in Sweden, four in Finland and others in Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and Austria.
Bodycote said the privately-owned Brukens would make profit before tax of 85 million crowns (7.8 million pounds) in the year ended December 31, 1996.

"Brukens is an excellent company and a strategic fit for us," Bodycote managing director John Chesworth said. He said the buy, due to take place on January 2 next year, would materially enhance Bodycote's earnings from the outset, before taking account of possible savings from rationalisation.
Bodycote shares rose 24 pence to 735 following the news.
